newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise further, global issues eyed.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise further, global issues eyed.

text.p: Argentine bonds ended higher again Wednesday with yet another strong upward spurt although with more selective buying than on Tuesday.

"The market is very firm. It is getting its impulse from the launch of the global bond," said a trader at a foreign bank. Argentina is due to place $2.0 billion in global bonds before the end of January, split between a five- and a 20-year issue.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 surged 3/4 to 89-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.25 to 125.30.

But unlike on Tuesday when peso and dollar issues alike rallied, peso issues did not follow the rise in dollar bonds this session as some investors thought the spreads between the two denominations had narrowed too much.
"The spreads corrected today," said another trader.

The trader said after this session's slow start, the market really took off as prices did not fall with U.S. Treasuries around noon because some players were caught short. "I would not dare to remain short in coming days," he added.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 5.48 percent from 5.38 percent.
